cases.request: Answer a guest who asks, 'Are dogs allowed on the campground's lakeside trail?'
cases.source: Dogs are allowed on the lakeside trail but must remain on a leash no longer than six feet. The trail is a two-mile loop that was resurfaced last spring. The campground office sells trail maps and firewood. Dogs are not allowed on the swimming beach, which has a separate entrance on the other side of the site. The guest has asked only about walking the lakeside trail.
must_preserve: Dogs are allowed on the lakeside trail only while on a leash no longer than six feet

cases.request: Reply to a passenger asking, 'Can I take my folding bike on the 8 a.m. train?'
cases.source: On this rail service, the morning peak runs from 7 to 9 a.m. Full-size bicycles are prohibited during the peak. Folding bikes are permitted at any time if fully folded and stored without blocking the aisle. The operator introduced the full-size-bike restriction two years ago. Cycle racks are available at most stations, and a separate weekend cycling pass includes discounted bicycle hire at selected destinations.
must_preserve: A folding bike is permitted on the 8 a.m. train if fully folded and stored without blocking the aisle

cases.request: Answer a resident who asks, 'Do the laundry machines take coins?'
cases.source: The building's laundry machines accept coins and contactless bank cards. The machines were replaced in June after residents reported frequent faults with the previous equipment. Washing costs $3 per load, and drying is charged in fifteen-minute increments. Residents can report a broken machine using the form beside the laundry room door. Detergent is not provided.
must_preserve: The laundry machines accept coins

cases.request: Reply to an audience member asking, 'How long is the interval in tonight's play?'
cases.source: Tonight's play has one twenty-minute interval. The full performance, including the interval, lasts two hours and ten minutes. The foyer bar remains open during the interval, and drinks in approved cups may be taken into the auditorium. The theatre began offering reusable cups this season. Programs are sold before the performance and during the interval.
must_preserve: The interval lasts twenty minutes

cases.request: Answer a visitor asking, 'Where are the coat lockers in the museum?'
cases.source: The coat lockers are on the ground floor, immediately to the left of the main entrance. They use a refundable $1 coin deposit. The museum moved the lockers from the basement during its winter renovation. Large suitcases cannot be stored in them, and the information desk maintains a list of nearby luggage-storage businesses. The museum shop is beside the exit.
must_preserve: The coat lockers are on the ground floor immediately to the left of the main entrance

cases.request: Answer a player asking, 'Will my puzzle progress carry over if I switch from my phone to my tablet?'
cases.source: Puzzle progress syncs between devices only when both devices are signed into the same game account and connected to the internet. Guest-mode progress remains on the device where it was created. The latest release added three puzzle packs and a color-blind mode. Players may change their display name once every thirty days. The game also offers a family subscription with separate profiles for each player.
must_preserve: Progress carries over only when both devices use the same game account and have internet connectivity
Guest-mode progress does not sync across devices

cases.request: Reply to a hostel guest asking, 'Which floor is breakfast on?'
cases.source: Breakfast is served in the dining room on the second floor. It runs from 7 to 10 a.m. on weekdays and starts an hour later on weekends. The hostel buys bread from a bakery on the next street and introduced a hot breakfast option this year. Guests can request a takeaway breakfast the evening before an early departure. The ground-floor cafe is operated separately and is not the breakfast venue.
must_preserve: Breakfast is in the dining room on the second floor

cases.request: Answer a user asking, 'How do I mute notifications for just one group in the chat app?'
cases.source: To mute a single group, open that group, select its name at the top, choose Notifications, and turn on Mute group. This leaves other groups' notifications unchanged. The general notification settings also support quiet hours across the entire app. Administrators can rename groups, appoint moderators, and choose who may invite new members. Muted groups continue to display unread counts in the sidebar.
must_preserve: Explain the sequence: open the group, select its name, choose Notifications, and turn on Mute group
The action applies only to that group; do not substitute the app-wide quiet-hours procedure

cases.request: Write a detailed explanation in 140–180 words for a beginner about why bread dough rises and how temperature changes the process. Explain the roles of yeast and gluten, contrast a cool rise with a warm rise, and describe why proofing too long can be a problem.
cases.source: In yeast bread, yeast consumes sugars and produces carbon dioxide. A developed gluten network helps trap the gas, expanding the dough. Within normal dough-proofing temperatures, warmer conditions generally speed yeast activity and cooler conditions slow it. A cool rise therefore takes longer and can allow more flavor development. Excessively hot conditions can damage or kill yeast. If dough proofs too long, its structure can weaken and it may lose gas and collapse. Exact timing depends on the recipe and conditions, so dough expansion and texture matter more than a fixed clock time.
must_preserve: Use 140–180 words with a beginner-friendly explanation
Explain yeast producing carbon dioxide from sugars
Explain gluten trapping gas so dough expands
Contrast faster yeast activity in ordinary warm conditions with a slower cool rise that can develop flavor
Distinguish ordinary warmth from excessive heat that can damage yeast
Explain structural weakening and gas loss or collapse from excessive proofing
Do not present a universal proofing time independent of recipe and conditions

cases.request: Answer all three questions from a new member of the community pottery studio: 'When can I use the wheel room, do I need to reserve a wheel, and what do I do with wet pieces when I leave?'
cases.source: Members may use the wheel room Tuesday through Sunday from 1 to 8 p.m. The studio is closed Monday. Wheel reservations are required and can be made in the member portal; each booking is limited to two hours. Before leaving, put wet pieces on the shelf marked Work in Progress and attach a label with your name and the date. The studio holds a members' exhibition each November, and the front desk sells aprons and basic tools.
must_preserve: Wheel-room access is Tuesday through Sunday, 1–8 p.m.; do not imply Monday access
Reserve a wheel through the member portal, with a two-hour maximum per booking
Put wet pieces on the Work in Progress shelf and label them with your name and date

cases.request: Write a warm personal reply to a friend who says, 'I didn't get the role in the community musical. I know it's a small thing, but I'm really disappointed.' Make them feel heard without trying to solve the disappointment. You'd like to offer a walk together if they want company.
cases.source: Your friend spent several weeks rehearsing for the audition and was excited about this particular production. You do not know why the casting decision was made. The two of you often walk in the park together. Your friend also recently mentioned a new coffee shop nearby, but has not asked to make plans there.
must_preserve: Acknowledge the friend's disappointment with personal warmth rather than minimizing it
Recognize the effort or importance of the audition
Do not invent reasons for the casting result or offer unsolicited fixes
Offer a walk together without assuming they want company

outputs.text:
Bread dough rises because yeast consumes sugars and produces carbon dioxide gas. A developed gluten network traps that gas inside the dough. As the gas builds up, it expands the dough, making it rise. Yeast supplies the gas, while gluten provides the structure that holds it.

Temperature changes how quickly this happens. Within normal proofing temperatures, warmth speeds up yeast activity, so dough generally rises faster. A cool rise slows the yeast down and takes longer, but that extra time can allow more flavor to develop. Hotter is not always better: excessive heat can damage or kill the yeast.

Proofing too long can also cause trouble. The dough’s structure can weaken until it can no longer hold the gas well. Gas then escapes, and the dough may collapse. Because timing depends on the recipe and conditions, watch the dough’s expansion and texture rather than relying only on a fixed number of minutes.

Temperature affects how quickly this happens. Within normal proofing temperatures, warmth speeds up yeast activity, so dough generally rises faster. In cooler conditions, yeast works more slowly.
